name: network-graph
purpose: Accessible SVG network graph: nodes and edges laid out by a deterministic force-directed simulation (seeded; it settles, then stops). The settling animates only when animation is allowed and the user has not asked for reduced motion. Node groups get palette colors and marker shapes; nodes can be pinned by dragging or with Shift+Arrow; zoom and pan use the shared chart zoom. Arrow keys move between connected nodes, neighbors are highlighted on focus, and the data table is an adjacency list.
whenToUse: Relationships between entities: team collaboration, service dependencies, referral networks.
Spotting clusters, hubs, and isolated nodes.
whenNotToUse: Hierarchies: use Org Chart or Treemap.
Flows with quantities between stages: use Funnel Chart or Bar Chart.
Thousands of nodes: a force layout becomes a hairball; aggregate first.
responsive: The width follows the container (ResizeObserver); the layout is fitted to the plot keeping its aspect ratio, so it never overflows. Labels (auto) are shown for up to 50 visible nodes. Wide data tables scroll in a focusable region.
rtl: direction rtl puts node labels on the left of the nodes. The layout itself is not mirrored (positions have no reading direction); arrow keys are spatial.
theme: Nodes use their group palette slot (--aui-chart-<n>) and marker shape with a color-surface outline; edges use color-chart-axis; pinned nodes get a dashed color-text outline; the focused or hovered neighborhood stays opaque while the rest fades. Forced colors: CanvasText nodes and edges, Highlight for the neighborhood and focus.
security: All text (title, description, labels, values, legend, tooltip, table) is set with textContent; SVG is built with createElementNS; positions and per-item colors are written through the CSSOM (style.setProperty) or as SVG geometry. No innerHTML, no style attributes, no inline handlers: works under style-src without unsafe-inline and require-trusted-types-for.
dataHandling: Renders the data it is given; no persistence, network access, or telemetry. Values are not logged; validation errors name the option, never its value.

budgets.metric: NetworkGraph.create with 150 nodes and 300 edges, synchronous layout (reduced motion) and the first render

performance.testedScale: Designed for up to about 300 nodes and 1,000 edges; at most 1,000 nodes and 5,000 edges are accepted (the layout cools faster above 300 nodes, since repulsion is O(n^2) per step).

limitations: Pairwise repulsion is O(n^2) per step; very large graphs lay out slowly.
Dragging pins a node where it is dropped; other nodes keep their positions until the layout runs again (relayout() or new data).
Straight edges only; parallel edges overlap.
unsupported: Editing nodes and edges by pointer.
antiPatterns: Encoding groups by color only and hiding the legend (marker shapes and the table carry the group too).
Rendering thousands of nodes without aggregation.
